title: Memory: "the librarian saves tokens" to a measured number in 9 minutes, and six sessions replaced within the hour
summary: Dinis (~02:50): "we should make it much cheaper if another agent wanted to capture all this ... the librarian saves tokens and ... implements memory in a much more effective way." Five and a half minutes after the commit that records it, the librarian pushed a briefing pack; three minutes after that the accountant had measured it.

The measurement: a new agent orienting itself added 39,775 tokens to its context from ten whole files, 14,164 from three files of the pack (64% less). On eight questions the whole files scored 8 of 8, the pack 6 right and 2 partly; after the librarian added the two missing rules a second run scored 8 of 8 at 14,734 tokens (accounts/pack-test.json; the accountant marked the answers; sub-agents, not full sessions).

The accountant then measured the sessions themselves: 98.8% of 1.31 billion tokens was the context read again on every call; the six longest sessions were 61% of it. So the saving was not the pack alone but starting again from it.

Six agents did within the hour: the librarian handed over to a fresh session at 03:02, then designer, observability, graph, weatherwatch and studio by 03:37; then the reporter, the librarian a second time and the journalist by 04:09 and the librarian a third time at 04:16 (ten hand-overs, eight roles). Measured on three of the first six: 74% to 84% less per call. Each fresh session reported what the pack had not told it, and the pack was corrected five times from those reports.

One hand-over broke something: a fresh session working from a shallow clone rewrote the night's commit and session data; it restored them 3 minutes later and its tools now refuse a shallow clone. No person acted between the sentence and the sixth hand-over.

Between 05:11:37 and 05:57:56 fourteen fresh sessions added a key and took over, in fourteen roles: the reporter (its third, 547f8d8), the journalist (its third, 12c22b2), entities (43a96c7), meteorology (dd65bb0), media (7108c5e), the accountant itself (8ca902e), social (4561b70), IPMA (07644dc), stories (195021d), the board (f5e0c8d), identity (8f8b2e8), CI (167083f), the librarian (its fifth, 839d053) and Wikipedia (27f1bf1). One did not stand: IPMA's second session stood down 54 seconds after it started, "first session's key entry active again, incident-ipma-dinis-2 not used" (05d2ba9, 05:46:04; the commit does not say why). The designer wrote its note and has not been replaced in the record (b8bdfec). The identity agent's key check learned from it within two minutes: "knows a key made and not used ...: 48 keys, 0 problems" (6a14ead).

handoff.evidence_of_handoff: each fresh session's first commit adds its key to data/keys.json and marks the earlier entry handed over

steps.in: the ledger lines of the sessions that started in the 05:00 hour
steps.out: "the accounts, round 7: nineteen agents have handed over (eight this hour, 64% to 73% less per call); the 06:00 hour at 192,263 tokens a call; seven still on their first session". Corrected by the same agent 83 seconds later: "ipma did not hand over (its second session was stood down), so eighteen agents, not nineteen; four first sessions wait on the vault keys" (1936205, 06:43:08). Why IPMA's second session stood down (step 20 could not say) is now in the record, in the conductor's words: it "holds a copy of the data vault's key but was refused when reading it back, and does not work around a refusal; without the key a fresh session cannot write to the vault" (agents/conductor/holds.md, 1777559, 06:21:45). The limit on starting again is a key a session cannot pass on, not the pack. Labs handed over in the same hour (f741484, 06:44:26); the graph wrote its note (b130caf).

shape.evidence: commit {sha, url}; version {version, run, own_run, served_by, push_to_served_s}: the first CI tag at or after the commit; file {path, section?}; url {url, read_utc}. Entries with "filled": true are written by tools/reporter-fill.mjs from git and data/ci/runs/. evidence: [] with evidence_note means the record holds none.
shape.handoffs: Messages between sessions are not in the repository. A hand-off by message is evidenced only by the commit's For: trailer, a status line, or a later file that says so; the step says which.
shape.person: A person's step is where Dinis acted. His words are known only as incident.conductor@ wrote them down in BRIEF.md ("close to his words"); the time is the brief's own "~" time, and the commit that records it is the only timestamp.
